human_tolerance.notes: One of the commonest feeder birds in North America, especially in winter; it takes Niger seed from suburban feeders and builds its cup nest in the thistle, teasel and ragweed stems a weedy garden is full of.

phases.name: breeding
phases.note: A clutch of four to six bluish-white eggs, incubated by the female alone; the chicks hatch 12 to 14 days after incubation begins and the male feeds them for up to three weeks after they fledge.

phases.name: flocking
phases.note: Outside the breeding season birds gather in flocks and shift onto weed and grass seed, which is why they are so numerous at feeders in winter.

vocalizations.description: A series of musical warbles and twitters, often with a long note; can last up to two or three seconds.
The flight call, per-twee-twee-twee or ti-di-di-di, punctuated by silent periods; also described as a tsee-tsi-tsi-tsit in flight.

Two nesting defence calls: a sweet call that rallies other goldfinches to the nest and distracts a predator, and a bearbee that tells nestlings to crouch and go quiet. Birds do not attack a predator in the territory; alarm calling is their only reaction.

range.note: Country list reduced from the article's range description: breeds across Canada and the United States, is resident in the south of both, and reaches Mexico; the Central and South American parts of the range are left off rather than guessed.

traits.locomotion_modes.note: A small perching finch that hops when foraging and flies everywhere else; taken from the frequent flight call and from foraging in weeds and at feeders.

traits.nest_type.note: The nest is a well-built cup of plant down and grass, usually tied to thistle, teasel or ragweed stalks.

traits.lifespan_y.note: 'The oldest known American goldfinch was 10 years and 5 months old.' No mean is given, so 2.0 years is a judgement by analogy to other small, heavily predated passerines in this repository, pending a better source.

traits.diet.note: 'Its diet consists of the seeds from a wide variety of plants', and 'seeds represent most of their diet'; insects are taken mainly for nestlings. Shares are a judgement.

traits.social.note: 'Two or three pairs may group their territories together in a loose colony', and birds gather in flocks outside the breeding season; the group-size range is a judgement.

traits.activity_pattern.note: Authored: a day-active feeder and seed-forager; the source does not state an activity pattern explicitly.

traits.defense.note: 'Birds do not act aggressively toward predators within their territory; their only reaction is alarm calling', and the defensive calls described are all aimed at deterring a predator rather than attacking it.

traits.wariness.note: Judgement: it will feed in the open at a suburban feeder within a few feet of people.

habitat.use.note: It forages in weed and grass seed heads, often well above the ground, and comes down to feeders; the split between weed-stalk and ground foraging is a judgement.

habitat.shelter_tag.note: Roosts and sings from thistle, teasel, ragweed and from shrubs and small trees; 'perch' is the matching drawable shelter tag.

habitat.resources.note: Seed-dominated diet, a weedy-plant nesting substrate, perching in shrubs and feeder use; weights are judgement.

habitat.human_tolerance.note: 'It will eat at bird feeders provided by humans, particularly in the winter months, preferring Niger seed'.

seasonal.strategy.note: The article describes southern birds as resident and northern birds as migratory, gathering in winter flocks; PartialMigration with a moderate winter fraction.

seasonal.winter_fraction.note: Judgement: many southern-breeding birds stay put all year, so most of the population winters within its breeding range.

seasonal.phases.note: The article gives clutch size and incubation and fledging intervals but no calendar window for laying; the breeding and flocking windows here are a judgement placed on the North American breeding season.

seasonal.life_stages.note: 'the chicks hatch 12-14 days after incubation begins' and the male feeds them 'for up to three weeks after fledging'; 21 days is the mid-fledging-plus-feeding period and the 0.82 scale is a judgement.

vocalizations.song.note: 'The song is a series of musical warbles and twitters, often with a long note.'

vocalizations.perseet.note: 'The call made during flight is "per-twee-twee-twee", or "ti-di-di-di", punctuated by the silent periods', also rendered as 'tsee-tsi-tsi-tsit'.

vocalizations.alarm.note: 'There are two defense calls made by adults during nesting; a sweet call made to rally other goldfinches to the nest and distract predators, and a bearbee used to signal to the nestlings to quiet them and get them to crouch down in the nest to become less conspicuous.'

look.note: 'the body of the male is a brilliant lemon yellow, a color produced by carotenoid pigments from plant materials in its diet, with a striking jet black cap and white rump that is visible during flight'; palette, proportions and box placement are judgement.

behavior.note: Authored parameters for the shared perching-songbird program, with the song standing in for the warbled song and seed as the food tag.
